chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Muhammad b. Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Layla from Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:
Whoever has been allotted foolishness, faith will be veiled from him.

key_terms.الإيمان: Iman (faith) - sincere belief in God and His guidance, requiring both knowledge and righteous character
key_terms.الخرق: Khurq (foolishness/recklessness) - opposite of hilm (forbearance); denotes lack of prudence and rash behavior
key_terms.حجب: Hujiba (was veiled/obstructed) - passive voice indicating divine decree; faith is screened away from the foolish

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between foolishness and faith according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a direct causal relationship between foolishness (khurq) and the deprivation of faith (iman). The word 'khurq' denotes recklessness, lack of prudence, and foolish behavior -- the opposite of 'hilm' (forbearance). The hadith uses the passive voice ('qusima' -- was allotted, and 'hujiba' -- was veiled) to indicate that both foolishness and its consequence are within the framework of divine decree. When foolishness takes hold of a person's character, it becomes an obstacle to genuine faith, because faith requires wisdom, reflection, and disciplined conduct -- qualities incompatible with recklessness.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Muhammad b. `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Layla from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as). He said:
Whoever has a share of foolishness, faith will be obstructed from him.
